title: Is That €60 Each or in Total?
prerequisites: Understand simple prices and group numbers.
Recognise basic yes-no questions with be.
observable_outcome: The learner asks whether a quoted price is per person or total, then confirms the amount and group size in one checking question.
learning_objective: Clarify whether a quoted price is per person or total, then confirm the amount and group size accurately.

scenario.setting: A tour desk before a group booking.
scenario.prompt: The agent says: The tour is €60. Your group has three adults. The quote does not say whether €60 is for each person or for the whole group.
scenario.puzzle: What must you clarify before paying, and how can you confirm the final amount?
scenario.privacy_note: The tour, people, and prices are fictional teaching data.

model.clarify: Is that €60 per person or €60 in total?
model.confirm: So that is €180 in total for three people, right?
model.neutral_variant: Just to check, is the €60 price for each person or for the whole group?

language_focus.grammar: With be, put is before the subject: Is that ...? An alternative question presents two possibilities joined by or: Is that €60 per person or €60 in total? A checking statement can end with right? in neutral informal conversation.
language_focus.meaning: Per person means for each person. In total means the whole amount for everyone together. The two phrases change the cost, so repeat both the final amount and the group size.
language_focus.appropriateness: The direct alternative question is clear and neutral at a tour desk. Just to check softens the question. Avoid asking only Is that right? before stating the amount you want confirmed.
language_focus.detail_language: For three people names the group size. If the price is €60 per person, three people cost €180 in total. The arithmetic illustrates the language consequence; the target skill is clarification and readback.

choice_activity.prompt: The agent says only: The tour is €60. What is unclear?

options.text: Whether €60 is per person or total
options.feedback: Correct. The quote gives an amount but not its scope: one person or the whole group.
The agent is offering the tour. The missing detail is what the €60 price covers.
The group size is already clear. You need to connect the quoted price to each person or everyone together.

options.text: Is that €60 per person or €60 in total?
options.feedback: Correct. The question names both possible meanings and lets the agent choose one.

options.text: Just to check, is the €60 price for each person or for the whole group?
options.feedback: Also correct. Just to check softens the question; each person and the whole group explain the two meanings.
The meaning may be guessed, but the standard full question needs be before the subject: Is that ...?

slot_activity.prompt: Match each detail to its confirmation slot.

feedback.rate: Correct. This is the amount for each individual person.
feedback.group size: €60 per person is a rate, not the number of people.
feedback.final total: €60 is not the whole cost when three people each pay €60.

feedback.rate: Three people is the size of the group, not a price for each person.
feedback.group size: Correct. This states how many people are included in the calculation.
feedback.final total: Three is a count of people, not the final amount.

feedback.rate: €180 is the combined amount here, not the price for one person.
feedback.group size: €180 is an amount, not a number of people.
feedback.final total: Correct. This is the whole amount for all three people.

production_task.scenario: A kayak hire worker says: The lesson is €45. You are booking for two people. The worker explains that €45 is per person.
production_task.instruction: Write one question that clarifies the price scope. Then write one complete confirmation with the total and the group size.
acceptable_responses: Is that €45 per person or €45 in total? So that is €90 in total for two people, right?
Just to check, is €45 for each person or for both of us? So the total is €90 for two people. Is that correct?
rubric: I asked whether the price was for each person or the whole group.
I used a complete question with is before the subject.
I repeated the group size and invited confirmation.
production_task.valid_variants: Per person and for each person are equivalent here. In total, altogether, and for the whole group can work when the amount clearly covers everyone. A different final wording is acceptable if it repeats the amount and group size.

review_prompt: Tomorrow, explain the difference between per person and in total. Then make one alternative question with or and one complete price readback.

scenes.title: See the unclear quote
scenes.caption: The tour is €60. Your group has three adults.
scenes.explanation: A tour kiosk opens. One €60 tag slides in beside three traveller cutouts, but no scope label appears.

scenes.title: Name the two meanings
scenes.caption: Does €60 mean per person or in total?
scenes.explanation: The €60 tag pivots between one-person and whole-group paper layers. A labelled or hinge joins the two options.

scenes.title: Ask the alternative question
scenes.caption: Is that €60 per person or €60 in total?
scenes.explanation: A layered speech card unfolds. The two price-scope choices slide into the same question.

scenes.title: Apply the reply
scenes.caption: It is €60 per person.
scenes.explanation: The single quote duplicates into three €60 person-tags. Each tag lands beside one traveller.

scenes.title: Confirm amount and group
scenes.caption: So that is €180 in total for three people, right?
scenes.explanation: Three €60 coins stack into a €180 receipt. Three labelled people and a check mark remain visible.

scenes.title: Your kayak booking
scenes.caption: €45 each becomes €90 in total for two people.
scenes.explanation: Two kayak cutouts enter. Two €45 tags combine into a €90 receipt. Ask, then confirm before paying.

visual.title: Clarify the price scope, then confirm the whole booking
visual.alt_text: A colourful layered papercut flow. One €60 quote branches to per person or in total. The reply selects per person. Three €60 person-tags then combine into a €180 total for three people, followed by a confirmation check.
visual.prose: First notice that a price without a scope can have two meanings. Ask whether it is per person or in total. Use the reply with the group size to identify the whole amount. Then repeat the total and number of people and invite confirmation.
